monetization.wtp_evidence: Buyers pay for broad access platforms: Vendr reports a StrongDM median of ~$33k/yr across 58 purchases, and its buyer guide shows a ~$71k average contract value that large deals skew upward. IAM itself is usable at no additional charge per AWS's RDS docs, so the per-client auth plumbing has no paid line item to displace.

monetization.bundling_note: AWS already ships IAM auth for RDS/MSK/Redshift/API Gateway plus free open-source signers in every major language and RDS Proxy, so remaining gaps get closed by AWS or OSS maintainers.

paid_market_gaps.gap: Popular third-party clients and ORMs (Prisma, kafka-go, ArgoCD) lack native AWS IAM auth; vendors don't sell client-side fixes.
RDS IAM auth caps around 200 new connections/second; the AWS workaround, RDS Proxy, adds per-vCPU cost.
Access proxies that broker IAM DB auth (Teleport, StrongDM) are quote-based or seat-minimum, heavy for small teams.
API Gateway IAM (SigV4) invocation from generic tooling relies on per-tool support that is often missing.

monetization.summary: Little standalone opening: the need is client-library plumbing that AWS and open source fill for free. Money only exists inside broader access-proxy platforms (Teleport, StrongDM), a crowded segment; at most a developer-tool feature, not a startup.

threat.reason: Short-lived IAM tokens replace static database and service passwords, shrinking the window for stolen-credential reuse.
